slot.brief: Given a compound statement involving ∧, ∨, negations, select the logically equivalent simplified form.

stem: The proposition $¬[(p∧¬q)∨(¬p∧r)]∧(p∨¬q)$ is logically equivalent to

verdicts.working: For p=1, the proposition reduces to q; for p=0, it reduces to ¬q∧¬r. Thus it is (p∧q)∨(¬p∧¬q∧¬r).

working:
$¬[(p∧¬q)∨(¬p∧r)]∧(p∨¬q)=[(¬p∨q)∧(p∨¬r)]∧(p∨¬q)$. For $p=1$: $q$; for $p=0$: $¬q∧¬r$.

Independent check: For p=1, the proposition reduces to q; for p=0, it reduces to ¬q∧¬r. Thus it is (p∧q)∨(¬p∧¬q∧¬r).
